title: Citeck Permissions Schema
description: Schema for Citeck permissions configuration files
x-intellij-html-description:
Schema for Citeck permissions configuration files

  • Used to define permissions for entity types and their attributes
  • Supports matrix and rules-based permission configuration

id.description: Unique identifier for the permissions configuration
id.x-intellij-html-description:
Unique identifier for the permissions configuration

  • Must be unique within the system

typeRef.description: Reference to the entity type these permissions apply to
typeRef.x-intellij-html-description:
Reference to the entity type these permissions apply to

  • Format: emodel/type@[type-id] or, for a type that lives in a workspace, emodel/type@[workspace]:[type-id]
  • Example: emodel/type@endpoint, emodel/type@test-c323:endpoint

permissions.x-intellij-html-description:
Permission configuration for the document/entity

  • Defines who can access and modify the entity itself

rules.description: Additional permission rules for more complex conditions
rules.x-intellij-html-description:
Additional permission rules for more complex conditions

  • Used when permission logic cannot be expressed with a simple matrix
  • Allows conditional permission granting based on attributes or other factors

attributes.description: Permission configurations for specific attributes. A NON-EMPTY section is a closed list on the platform: every model attribute it does not name becomes read-only for everybody and a write to it is silently dropped. List only the attributes with their own rule; the code gives every other attribute of the type a copy of the record-level permissions block — on a new section only: an existing matrix that already lists attributes is kept as it is, and a listed attribute is never dropped (to make it follow the record, give it a block equal to the record-level one). A listed attribute whose block equals the record-level block follows the record: on a change of the record level leave that block as it is, the code gives it the new record-level block; an attribute with a block of its own is not touched. An attribute's WRITE works only where the role may also WRITE the record: the platform checks the record-level access first and refuses the whole change before it looks at the attributes, so give the role WRITE on that attribute only and leave its record-level cell as the user asked: the code raises the cell itself and keeps the role READ on every other attribute — their blocks become the record block plus an unconditional REVOKE WRITE rule for the role (a restricted copy); leave a restricted copy as it is, and to let the role change that attribute remove its REVOKE rule; WRITE on the record also lets the role delete the record. The attributes an aspect of the type brings (<prefix>:<id>) are attributes of the type too: the code completes them like the others.
attributes.x-intellij-html-description:
Permission configurations for specific attributes

  • Keys are attribute identifiers
  • Values are permission definitions for each attribute
  • Allows fine-grained access control at the attribute level

rules.description: Additional permission rules for this attribute

x-intellij-enum-metadata.WRITE: Permission for read and write access
Permission for read and write access

permissionMatrix.x-intellij-html-description:
Matrix of permissions based on roles and statuses

  • System roles:
    • EVERYONE - virtual role that includes all users. Assignees for this role are always empty, but if EVERYONE gets permissions via matrix, they apply to all users in the system.
  • System statuses:
    • EMPTY - empty status. Useful for private entities that aren't readable by all users. Empty status may occur if a process for a case is not found or process start operation hasn't completed yet.
    • ANY - every status, but it can only RAISE access: the platform takes the status cell (an unset one is READ) and unites it with the ANY cell, so ANY: WRITE grants WRITE everywhere, while ANY: NONE closes nothing and ANY: READ changes nothing; the code expands ANY: NONE into NONE in every status cell the row leaves unset (and EMPTY) before the deploy, keeping the cells set explicitly (a type with no statuses: the column EMPTY).

roles.description: Roles to which the rule applies
roles.x-intellij-html-description:
Roles to which the rule applies

  • System roles:
    • EVERYONE - virtual role that includes all users. Assignees for this role are always empty, but if EVERYONE gets permissions via matrix, they apply to all users in the system.

permissions.description: Permissions that this rule grants or revokes

statuses.description: Statuses in which the rule applies. An empty list [] means every status, the terminal ones and a record without a status included. ANY is a matrix column, not a rule status: the platform compares a rule's statuses literally, so ANY would never match; the code writes [] (every status) in place of a list that names ANY.
statuses.x-intellij-html-description:
Statuses in which the rule applies

  • System statuses:
    • EMPTY - empty status. Useful for private entities that aren't readable by all users. Empty status may occur if a process for a case is not found or process start operation hasn't completed yet.
    • Every status: an empty list []. ANY is a matrix column only: a rule compares statuses literally, so the code writes [] in place of a list that names ANY.

condition.description: Predicate condition that must be satisfied for the rule to apply
condition.x-intellij-html-description:
Predicate condition for rule application

  • Simple conditions use format: {"t": "eq", "att": "attributeName", "val": "value"}
  • Complex conditions can use nested predicates

type.description: Type of rule (allow or revoke permissions)

x-intellij-enum-metadata.ALLOW: Grants the specified permissions when condition is met
x-intellij-enum-metadata.REVOKE: Removes the specified permissions when condition is met
